RPGME TEST RUN, GAME 5, 18 NOVEMBER 2026

One couple, nine paths the first four games never took

Robin made a game on her phone for Sam, her fiancé(e). Sam is nonbinary and uses they/them. Above are Sam and Robin as they look in the finished game, and the couple picture the site painted from Robin's words.

WHAT WE TESTED, AND WHAT HAPPENED

Seven paths worked. Two broke, and one of those reached the finished game.

BROKENA partner who uses they/themThe chat switched Sam to "she" because of the best friend's pronoun. Our buyer fixed it, so the finished game is right.
BROKEN, IN THE GAMENo pet, so a favorite animalThe red panda became an orange cat in the game, and Sam says the garbled sentence out loud.
WORKED, WRONG WORDSThe couple photo described in wordsThe picture was painted, but the chat said "Couldn't conjure the photo".
WORKED"None of these, try again" on looksIt asks what to change. Sam's final look has the undercut, hoops and nose ring asked for.
WORKEDChange an answerThe song changed to "Landslide", and the finished game uses it. The button was not always on screen.
WORKEDLooks picked by sightOur buyer now sees the look pictures. Both people are dressed in the game.
WORKEDPhotos where both people look downThe site accepted both, and the looks match the people.
WORKEDFiancé(e) and a typed occasionBoth saved word for word. The engagement got only "Noted!".
WORKED"No special keepsake"Saved as "They do not have a special keepsake".
BROKENTurns 9 to 48

The chat switched Sam from "they" to "she" because of someone else's pronoun

Robin set Sam's pronouns at the start. Almost forty turns later she described the best friend with "she", and the chat applied that to Sam.

1Robin tells the chat to call Sam "they".
2Robin describes Marisol, the best friend. The chat now calls Sam "she".
FROM THE CHAT LOG, WORD FOR WORD (BETWEEN TWO SCREENSHOTS)
GAME MASTER
Who's Sam's best friend? Tell me their name and what they're like.
ROBIN
Marisol! She's a pastry chef with a nose ring who laughs louder than anyone in any room.
GAME MASTER
Got it, I'll use she/her for Sam from now on.
3The next questions call Sam "her".

A better way: change a person's pronoun only from the pronoun question about that person. Never take it from an answer about someone else.

BROKENTurns 49 to 54

Fixing it took a hidden step

Our buyer wrote the correction into its next answer. The chat misread it, and the real fix came only from tapping the old answer.

1Robin writes "Sam uses they/them, not she/her". The chat offers to change Sam's name.
2Robin taps her old pronoun answer, which now reads "She". The chat asks the right question.
3Sam is "they" again. We found no line in the finished game that calls Sam "she".

A better way: when a buyer writes a pronoun correction, offer a button such as "Use they/them for Sam".

BROKEN, IN THE GAMETurns 35 to 37, and the finished game

Sam's favorite animal, a red panda, became an orange cat

With no pet, the chat asks for the partner's favorite animal, which becomes the sidekick. Robin answered: "Red pandas! Sam has a whole sticky note collection of them mixed in with the cats."

1The chat pastes Robin's whole sentence back in, in lower case, as the animal.
2It then calls the sidekick "the cat".
3In the finished game, Juniper is a cat. Sam says the sentence out loud, and a habit nobody gave appears.
LINES FROM THE FINISHED GAME
SAM
It's my Red pandas! Sam has a whole sticky note collection of them mixed in with the cats.
VELKA, THE SHOPKEEPER
It's just Juniper, that red panda over there.
All she does is brag that she always knows the way home.

A better way: read the animal ("red panda") out of the answer, confirm it with a button, and use a red panda sprite or say there is none.

Our buyer changed Sam's favorite song from "Dreams" to "Landslide" after the inside joke question. The "Change an answer" button was not on screen at that moment, so it tapped its old answer in the chat.

1The chat asks what to save instead.
2It confirms the change and goes back to the next question.

THE FINISHED GAME

The game was ready at 10:40 PM. Three of the four checks pass.

Robin tapped Build It! at 10:09 PM, and the game was published 30 minutes later, with no billing hold this time. These checks read the finished game's file.

WHERE TO START

Fix these three first, because each one puts wrong facts into a gift

Pronouns stay putOnly the pronoun question about a person may change that person's pronoun. Offer a clear fix button.
The right animalSave "red panda", not the sentence. Use the right sprite, and never invent a habit.
Say what really happenedShow the couple picture when it arrives, instead of "Couldn't conjure the photo".
